Its precondition is STALE: Phase D (decoy flicker on the LCD, sub-channel 4 = bus EM) was bench-tested 2026-06-09 and FAILED (repaint-limited at 20 MHz, decoys readable; `docs/archive/work-todo-retired-2026-07-19.md:2482`), `decoy-frames` stays OFF, so sub-channel 4 currently has NO countermeasure on the shipping panel — this proposal is the first candidate for it and is distinct from #260's channel; D-04 should be filed as its own issue and cross-linked, or #260 re-scoped. (2) gh #237 OPEN still frames the surface as SSD1306 and asks for the §7.10 threat-model row; D-04 should be bound to it. (3) gh #784 OPEN (medium): the restore-wizard letter row renders typed seed letters via `Item::Text` on a non-forced frame, bypassing `blit_secret_run` entirely — any constant-weight colour pair applied only to `Item::Secret` would miss that row until #784 lands; the two should be sequenced. Technical nits on the proposal text: the "two-constant change" on the legacy path is slightly optimistic — `FG`/`BG` in `lcd.rs` are shared by public and secret glyphs (`blit_glyph` is called by both `public_glyph_cols` and `secret_glyph_cols` paths), so it needs a separate SECRET_FG/SECRET_BG pair plus a per-cell `set_window` whose command bytes are also on the bus between cells (content-independent today, keep it so). SPI runs 8-bit DSIZE, so the "equal first and last bit" constraint must be evaluated on the 16-bit word in transmit order (bit 15 first) and ideally per byte. Could not check: anything on glass (pq1 bench has no LCD; no TVLA receipt exists for the panel bus — the `make -C tools/sca glyph-leak` harness covers the CPU-side glyph fetch only).

feasible.reason: The proposal is realisable exactly as described (pure firmware, no hardware change, legacy path is a per-cell colour parameter + two constants, px path is a quantise-then-branchless-select in the compositor) and it genuinely removes the first-order weight/transition dependence of the MOSI stream and of the MCU's IO-driver switching current on the secret bit. Verified facts: lcd.rs:47-48/263-264 and raster.rs:170/font.rs:318 are as cited; trusted UI runs SPI1 at 20 MHz (spi_hw.rs:221), 8-bit frames MSB-first, pixels big-endian, so a per-16-bit-word constraint with equal bit15/bit0 is the right unit. A brute-force search over RGB565 confirms pairs satisfying equal HW + equal intra-word transitions + equal first/last bit with ~6:1 luminance contrast (e.g. 0x6790/0x186E, HW 7, 6 transitions). However it does NOT prevent the attack class it cites: Kuhn's FPD-link attack and Screen Gleaning are pattern-RESOLVING receivers (wideband demodulation at a harmonic of the bit clock), not weight-integrating observers. A near-field probe + SDR with ~20-40 MHz bandwidth recovers the serial bit pattern of each word, and equal weight/transition count leaves the two words trivially distinguishable; the ideal max-contrast pair from the search (0x6790/0x186E) differs in 14 of 16 bits, i.e. its difference waveform carries almost as much energy as 0xFFFF/0x0000. So the defence is 'raises cost / kills first-order HW-model leakage', not 'prevents'. It also does nothing for the panel source-driver current named in the threat (contrast is by design, and that channel is the periodic/averageable one). These are corrections, not a refutation: the proposal flags the logic-tap residual, names the TVLA gate, and its cost/kind/priority are in the right band.
feasible.corrections: 1. Narrow the threat claim: constant-weight/transition coding equalises only what an INTEGRATING observer sees (IO-driver supply current, narrowband EM energy per bit period). The cited attacks (Kuhn pet2004 FPD-link, Screen Gleaning) resolve the serial bit pattern; against them the relevant metric is the difference waveform fg XOR bg, i.e. Hamming DISTANCE, which the proposal's search does not constrain. Add minimal Hamming distance to the search objective subject to contrast: e.g. fg=0x0400 (G=32/63, L~0.36) vs bg=0x0002 (B=2/31, L~0.005) has HW 1 each, 2 transitions each, equal first/last bit, contrast ~7.5:1 and distance 2 — about 9 dB less difference energy than a distance-14 pair, mid-green on black, probably more legible than the tinted pair too. Even then a wideband receiver still resolves the two differing bit slots; state the result as cost-raising. 2. The 'averaged across the periodic refresh' framing is wrong for the MOSI channel: the NV3007 has its own GRAM, firmware writes each secret cell once (blit_glyph per cell / one px strip pass), so the bus leak is single-shot per cell. The channel that IS periodic (panel-internal 60 Hz scan, content-dependent source-driver column swings for as long as the word is shown) is not addressed at all, since luminance contrast is required; the 'constant lit field' option adds a subtractable offset and does not equalise per-column swing on a TFT (Trezor's oledInvert/oledSCA worked because OLED current is per-lit-pixel). For the panel channel the right lever is #260's constant-weight-row padding (complement pixels per row so fg/bg counts are row-constant), and this proposal should be explicitly paired with it rather than presented as its bus-level alternative. 3. px path: binarising the AA secret tier at 142-px panel height is a legibility risk; if a grey ramp is wanted, pick all levels from ONE (HW, transitions, first, last) class so every level satisfies the constraints and the ramp is monotonic in luminance (classes with many members exist, e.g. HW 7/(6,0,0)); the strip background under the secret union box must be pre-filled with the chosen bg, not 0x0000, or the box edge pixels break the invariant. 4. MCU-internal residual stays: the mask register (0xFFFF vs 0x0000) and the secret-coverage arithmetic still have secret-dependent Hamming weight on-core; this only equalises the stored/transmitted value. 5. Legacy FG/BG are used by public text too (lcd.rs:47-48 are global); implement as a per-call colour pair so public rows keep white-on-black and secret rows are visibly distinct. 6. Priority: P1 is defensible only with the D-10 TVLA harness run before/after (single-shot bus capture + panel-rail capture), otherwise P2; cost S is right for legacy, S-M for px once quantisation + bg pre-fill + tests are included. Verification requires an iota2 LCD module or an EVT unit (pq1 bench has no panel), as the proposal says.

vendor-claim.reason: The precedent and novelty claims survive. Trezor legacy really ships oledSCA row padding + an oledInvert band on the recovery-word screen (legacy/oled.c:455-473, legacy/firmware/layout2.c:836-837, legacy/firmware/pinmatrix.c:51-52 via oledSCAInside; commits 1c9fa5d3c6/9107731079/0e224644b6 2019-07, CHANGELOG 1.8.2 'OLED display security improvements'). Trezor core has no software pixel padding anywhere (grep of core/embed/rust/src/ui incl. layout_caesar/component/share_words.rs returns nothing) and the OLED models T2B1/T3B1 instead call consumption_mask_randomize() from display_refresh (core/embed/io/display/vg-2864/display_driver.c:415-417, core/embed/models/{T2B1,T3B1}/model.toml:5) — a TIM PWM power mask, not a bus-level encoding; T2T1/T3T1 drive the ST7789 over FMC/i8080 (core/embed/io/display/st-7789/display_io.c:80-113) with no countermeasure. Ledger did ship inverted-pixel boxes for PIN/recovery (Ledger blog 'oled-vuln' 2019-08-07: 'all sensitive information (recovery phrase, PIN digits) will be displayed within boxes in inverted pixel mode'; Nano S 1.6.0 notes 2019-11-13: 'screen jitter and partial screen inversion'). No vendor found shipping equal-Hamming-weight / equal-transition colour pairs on an SPI TFT, so novelty='beyond' (vendor-relative) holds. Repo evidence verified: secure/src/ui/lcd.rs:47-48 FG=0xFFFF/BG=0x0000 and :262-264 branchless value mask; pqsigner-ui-px/src/raster.rs:166-179 blend_ct coverage-dependent colour (caller font.rs:318); gh #260 and #237 both OPEN priority:low with the stated bodies. Incomplete/imprecise points (below) do not reach refutation.
vendor-claim.corrections: 1) oledSCA is a MINIMUM-weight pad ('setting at least width pixels white', legacy/oled.c:452-455): it only adds pixels when the row has fewer than `width`; it is constant-weight only because the callers pick width = the max row count ('30 is the maximum pixels used for a pixel row in the BIP39 word abstract', layout2.c:835; pinmatrix.c:49-50 uses 56 > max 36 'to add some extra'). Say 'pad-to-maximum' rather than 'constant-weight'. Cited lines are 836-837, not 832-838. 2) LSB-006 (donjon.ledger.com/lsb/006) does NOT describe the mitigation at all (it only says power-shunt measurement on SSD1306 Nano S/X, CVE-2019-14354, fixes 'Q4 2019'); the inverted-box evidence is the Ledger blog post ledger.com/blog/oled-vuln (2019-08-07) and the Nano S 1.6.0 release notes (2019-11-13, 'screen jitter and partial screen inversion'). Correct the citation. 3) Missing Ledger follow-on precedent that strengthens the proposal's own 'risks' line: ledger.com/blog/new-pin-screen (2023-01-19) states 'no amount of physical noise could efficiently hide the dependency between the power consumption and the displayed data' on the newer Nano X / Nano S Plus panel and replaced inversion+noise with a PIN UI that makes 'the number of illuminated pixels in each row constant' — i.e. Ledger moved to constant-COUNT encoding (the #260 variant), which is the closest vendor analogue to D-04. 4) 'Trezor core deliberately dropped software padding in favour of the hardware mask' — the outcome is verified (no padding in core; USE_CONSUMPTION_MASK hook in vg-2864 display_refresh) but no commit/changelog evidences 'deliberately'; phrase as 'core never ported oledSCA; T2B1/T3B1 rely on consumption_mask_randomize() per refresh'. Also Trezor's CVE is CVE-2019-14353 (NVD), Ledger's is 14354; #237's '14354 class' is the Ledger number. 5) Academic precedent is understated and partly contradicts the proposal: the exact technique (two colours with equal per-channel transition count, equal pulse length, fg/bg differing only as a one-bit phase shift) IS Kuhn PET 2004 Fig. 5 lines 5-6; Kuhn found them unreadable at 350 MHz but 'suddenly ... readable' at a different centre frequency (285 MHz) and concluded 'the only effective software protection technique ... appears to be the addition of random bits to the color combinations', re-randomised at every glyph placement (never via a glyph cache). D-04 should be reframed as 'Kuhn line-5/6 constant-transition pairs' with Kuhn's random-bit jamming (fresh TRNG low bits per secret glyph blit, compatible with the CT fetch path) as the stronger variant, and the frequency-sweep failure mode added to the TVLA plan. 6) Screen Gleaning (arXiv 2011.09877, Liu et al.) supports only the threat class (EM from the display ribbon cable, ML digit recovery); it proposes shielding/encryption/filtered fonts, not weight equalisation — cite it as threat evidence only. 7) Additional vendor precedent: Coldcard v2.1.2 (blog.coinkite.com/noise-troll, 2019-08-07) added 'masking noise along the right hand side of the screen' on seed-word display and stopped echoing PIN digits — software decoy pixels on SSD1306, same class as Trezor legacy. 8) Repo nuance: docs/security/threat-model.md already HAS a §7.10 SCA section (line 323) — what is absent is a display-emanation ROW inside it; #237's wording is correct but any restatement must not say §7.10 is missing.
